summary: Quarterly health check covering usage growth, cost trends, recent incidents and roadmap alignment. Meridian is seeing steady adoption across clinical summarization and triage; cost is their primary open concern and security artifacts needed for upcoming procurement. Agreement to run a dedicated benchmark and to provide tailored pricing options.
transcript:
[00:00] Evan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a brief QBR and health check — 45 minutes. I'll kick off with usage highlights and then Maya will go into performance, and Liam will cover the CS items.

[00:22] Dr. Priya Malhotra: Great thanks. Quick note, we're on calls because finance wants to understand cost trajectory before the procurement window in May.

[00:35] Evan Park: Understood. To start, overall token usage month-over-month is up ~38% quarter over quarter, mostly driven by the clinical summarization flow and our triage assistant. The interesting bit is the inference pattern: short prompts high qps during business hours and long context sessions overnight.

[01:05] Carlos Rivera: Yeah we noticed that. Our autoscaler was struggling a bit at 11am spikes last week. There was like a 1200ms tail latency on a few requests.

[01:20] Maya Chen: Right, on that— we looked at the logs for the spike day. A couple things: 1) some of your routes are hitting longer sequence lengths than expected, which causes kernel selection to fall back to the slower path; 2) there's limited prefix caching on the triage flow because the prompts vary slightly so cache hit rate was only ~12%.

[01:46] Emma Li: When you say kernel selection, is that something Redwood controls on hosted? We have constraints on what can run in prod given our compliance team.

[01:54] Maya Chen: For Hosted and Dedicated the runtime selects kernels automatically based on model and seq-length distribution. For Private we provide the same runtime but you have control over kernel tuning if you want. We can document the decision table — I'll share the writeup.

[02:10] Dr. Priya Malhotra: Cost, though — our biggest ask. Our finance team flagged that cost per 1k tokens jumped ~22% month-over-month. What levers are available short term?

[02:25] Evan Park: Short-term levers: batching and better prefix caching, model variant routing (lower-cost quantized variants for non-critical paths), and lower-cost fallbacks for low-importance requests. We can show a quick sensitivity: increasing cache hit to 40% could reduce token compute by ~18%.

[02:46] Carlos Rivera: Does the Dedicated offering help with predictable unit cost? We're debating committed capacity vs hosted.

[02:53] Evan Park: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost profiles, yes — especially if you commit to baseline capacity. You get lower per-token compute, and options for burst capacity. We'll prepare a committed vs hosted TCO slide.

[03:08] Dr. Priya Malhotra: Security artifacts — Emma, what do we need to get this approved?

[03:15] Emma Li: SOC2 Type II evidence, KMS integration details, SSO/SAML integration notes and audit log retention windows. Also need encryption-at-rest details for model cache.

[03:24] Liam O'Connor: We can provide SOC2 scope docs and the KMS integration guide. For audit logs, Redwood Console supports per-route traces and token-level cost breakdowns; retention can be extended on an add-on. We'll send the security pack.

[03:39] Maya Chen: Back to reliability — there were two incidents last quarter flagged by your on-call. One was the autoscaler throttle during the 11am spike, the other was a degraded model variant fallback that returned lower-quality summaries for ~20 minutes. For the fallback, we saw the system reroute to a quantized variant when the primary model hit capacity.

[04:02] Dr. Priya Malhotra: That degraded summaries issue is the one that worried clinical ops. We can't have that in triage. Is there an SLA or can we pin a higher-quality model for that route?

[04:14] Evan Park: Yes you can pin routes to a model variant; we also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies with quality thresholds. For triage you probably want no-quantized fallback — we can set higher priority to keep it on the high-accuracy variant, or configure graceful degradation like returning a short "unable to summarize reliably" message instead of a bad summary.

[04:40] Carlos Rivera: Is there a way to run offline evals for these prompts before we accept a route change? We want regression testing.

[04:47] Maya Chen: Absolutely — Redwood Optimize has the eval harness. We can run your prompt sets against both variants and produce a quality delta report. If you share a representative set we'll run it against quantized and non-quantized variants.

[05:05] Dr. Priya Malhotra: We'll share two prompt sets — a production set and an edge-case set.

[05:10] Emma Li: Also, latency SLOs — what's realistic if we commit to Dedicated with a small baseline?

[05:18] Evan Park: With Dedicated and pinned model variants you can target 99th percentile latencies around 200–300ms for short prompts, depending on model size. For longer context sessions it's higher. We'll include historical dashboards in the packet.

[05:34] Carlos Rivera: About the autoscaler — can we tune the policy? We saw it wait to spin up nodes until CPU was high which caused tails.

[05:41] Maya Chen: Yes autoscaling is policy driven. We can shift to queue-length based scaling or target warm standby nodes for known traffic windows. Also, pre-warming and provisioned concurrency help with predictable spike handling.

[06:02] Dr. Priya Malhotra: Ok, procurement timeline: we need security artifacts by end of the week, pricing and TCO by next week, and a benchmark in the two weeks after.

[06:12] Evan Park: Sounds good. We'll prioritize the security packet and the dedicated pricing options.

[06:18] Liam O'Connor: I'll set up the benchmark session. Suggest we do a 60-minute dedicated run with your infra team so we can simulate the 11am spike and the overnight long-context jobs.

[06:31] Carlos Rivera: That would be good. We'll allocate infra to mirror production.

[06:36] Maya Chen: One tip — for your long-context jobs, consider chunked generation with KV caching between chunks rather than a single long forward. It keeps memory pressure down and helps the runtime choose faster kernels. I'll send a short note with examples.

[06:56] Dr. Priya Malhotra: On roadmap alignment — we have two features on our side: expanding summarization to multi-lingual notes and adding a secure on-prem fallback for extremely sensitive notes. How does Redwood support private/on-prem?

[07:10] Evan Park: We have Redwood Private — VPC/on-prem deployments with a private control plane. We can do customer-managed KMS and ensure audit logs never cross your network. There are deployment timelines and packaging considerations for air-gapped environments; we'll surface that in the security packet.

[07:25] Emma Li: For on-prem, what about model updates and kernel patches? We need patch cadence and a process for certifying updates.

[07:33] Maya Chen: For Private we provide an update bundle and a recommended cadence. You can opt into automatic updates or a staged release. We'll include our update policy and the patch notes cadence in the doc.

[07:46] Evan Park: Quick commercial note — we can offer a pilot Dedicated pack with 3 months of committed baseline at a trial discount if you want to validate cost predictability.

[07:56] Dr. Priya Malhotra: That could work — contingent on security review outcome.

[08:00] Liam O'Connor: Action recap: we'll send security pack, pricing + committed vs hosted TCO, scheduling benchmark. Maya will share KV cache tuning and quantization notes.

[08:12] Carlos Rivera: One last technical detail: you mentioned "KV cash" earlier in the docs — please make sure the guide says KV cache (typo), we had some confusion when we passed the doc to infra.

[08:22] Maya Chen: Noted, thanks. We'll proof the doc.

[08:27] Evan Park: Great. Any other questions?

[08:30] Dr. Priya Malhotra: No, that's all from me. Thank you.

[08:34] Evan Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items discussed.

[08:40] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors and colloquialisms; attendee labels captured as spoken. References: security pack (link to /redwood/security-pack.pdf), pricing spreadsheet (sent via email), benchmark run booking (calendar invite).
